features.title: Sync backlog items with a Notion data source
features.summary: Serves the backlog's backlog-provider Host API as the notion kind: a connection names the integration's bot and discovers the data sources it can see; a binding to a data source (or a database with one data source) pulls pages changed since a last_edited_time checkpoint in pages of 50, reads the title property, the page markdown as the body, a status property's groups (To-do, In progress, Complete) or a Status select as backlog statuses, a Tags multi-select, a Priority select and a Parent item relation, and writes them back through the binding's property names and value maps. Bodies change through one targeted update_content edit that never touches blocks markdown cannot show; comments flow both ways; deleting a linked item moves its page to the trash. Every request pins Notion-Version 2026-03-11, stays under three requests a second per connection and waits for Retry-After on 429 and 529.
features.currentSurface: Backlog settings › Remote sync › Add Notion connection (rendered by @dshfiles/backlog)

configuration.constraints: A secret:ALIAS reference resolved on the Host; empty falls back to NOTION_API_KEY.
Empty uses https://api.notion.com; any other http(s) base receives the key.
A data source id, a database id or notion.so URL with one data source, or empty for the only data source the integration sees.
A status or select property; empty finds a property named Status, State or Stage, then the only status property.
A multi-select property; empty finds Tags or Labels, then the only multi-select.
A select property; empty finds one named Priority.
Comma-separated priority=Name pairs (urgent=P0, high=P1); unmapped priorities match P0–P3, Critical, High, Medium, Low.
A relation property; empty finds Parent item or Parent.

failureModes: A key Notion refuses (401/403) or a page or database not shared with the integration (404) fails the call with its recovery: check the key, share the page with the integration.
A binding option naming a missing property or one of the wrong type fails with target-missing, naming the property and the type it needs.
A page whose markdown holds blocks the integration cannot see or the read truncated refuses a body edit that would cover them (unsupported); other fields still sync.
Still rate-limited after three Retry-After waits fails the call with a 429; the next pass retries from the same checkpoint.
Status options cannot be created through the API: a status the data source lacks is not written; a select status or priority creates its option.

externalDependencies.boundary: HTTPS requests to api.notion.com (or the connection's base URL) with the integration token as a bearer header and Notion-Version 2026-03-11: users/me, search, data_sources, databases, pages, pages/:id/markdown and comments.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/notion-fake.ts answers the same paths in memory through an HttpClient stand-in: one data source with status groups, tags, priority and parent properties, markdown bodies with truncation, comments, minute-granular last_edited_time and 429s on demand; the provider, its rate limiter and its decoding run for real.

verification.testName: names the bot and discovers data sources, pinning the API version on every request
binds a database URL to its only data source and refuses a wrongly typed property
pulls in pages with a last_edited_time checkpoint and still sees an edit within the same minute
reads status groups, tags, priority and parent, and writes them back through the same options
round-trips the markdown body with a targeted edit, and refuses to rewrite a truncated page whole
waits for Retry-After on a 429, then gives up after three retries
creates a page in the data source with properties and markdown, then trashes it
reports a refused key with its recovery and never echoes it

telemetry.testName: records one notion request span per call, with the operation and status only
